title: Attitudes towards and expectations on the role of artificial intelligence in the classroom among digitally skilled Finnish K-12 mathematics teachers
venue: LUMAT: International Journal on Math, Science and Technology Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines how digitally skilled Finnish K-12 mathematics teachers view artificial intelligence in school, with a focus on their expectations, attitudes, and perceived opportunities and risks. The authors frame AI adoption through the Will, Skill, Tool framework, arguing that teachers’ existing digital competence can serve as a proxy for readiness to adopt AI tools even when few have direct classroom experience with advanced AI systems.

The study used a web-based survey with 85 in-service mathematics teachers who taught across primary, lower secondary, and upper secondary levels in Finland. Respondents were recruited through teacher and university networks and completed questions about their current digital tool use, the pedagogical functions of those tools, their awareness of AI, possible classroom uses of AI, perceived risks, and attitudes toward AI in society and education. The survey was conducted in Swedish and Finnish before ChatGPT-3 was introduced.

Findings show that the teachers were already heavy users of digital mathematics resources and generally described themselves as technologically interested and experienced. They saw AI as potentially useful for individualized learning, scaffolding, differentiation, homework support, and teacher assessment tasks, but they also worried about privacy, data security, overreliance on algorithms, reduced student collaboration, and a shift away from core mathematical reasoning. Overall, the sample was characterized by interest and openness toward AI, tempered by ambivalence about risks. The authors conclude that these mathematics teachers appear likely to be early adopters of AI tools, though successful implementation would still require suitable tools, curriculum resources, and teacher preparation.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI / AI-tool category, including adaptive and individualized teaching materials, assessment support, exercise generation, and related AI-based classroom tools; no specific commercial product is named in the paper.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper surveyed K-12 mathematics teachers about their expectations, attitudes, and early experiences with AI-based tools in mathematics education, including potential uses such as individualized learning paths, homework support, assessment assistance, and automatic exercise generation.

findings.finding_summary: In a mixed-methods web survey of digitally skilled Finnish K-12 mathematics teachers (N=85), 78% thought AI-tools could create individual learning paths, 81% thought they could offer challenges for interested students, and 66% thought they could make it easier for the teacher to follow up and assess students. The paper reports no effect sizes because this was a survey of expectations rather than an intervention study.
findings.measure: Teacher survey responses on perceived potential uses of AI-tools in mathematics learning

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods survey study with descriptive and correlational analysis, not an intervention or causal design. The evidence is useful for understanding teacher attitudes and expectations, but it does not test AI-tool effects on student outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper indicates substantial perceived potential for AI tools in mathematics teaching, especially for personalization and assessment, but it provides no measured impact on learning or teaching performance. The impact is therefore plausible but unquantified.
